newsitem.title: USA: Snyder says SOCO plans China pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Snyder says SOCO plans China pipeline.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp said in a conference call that SOCO International Plc, the London-listed former unit of Snyder, which was spun off earlier this year, would build a pipeline from its Mongolian oilfields to China in 1999.
"They have a contract for an eight well programme next year and a pipeline the year after that," said John Snyder, Snyder Oil's chairman.
SOCO had a four well drilling programme for this year and is currently drilling an offset well to confirm a discovery that is flowing consistently at 600 barrels of oil per day.
"The rig will then drill a very large structure, which could be very meaningful and the biggest one so far," said Snyder.
The company was experiencing some problems with the quality of local concrete or pipes which may be damaging some of the structures and SOCO is looking into this.
Snyder said earlier this week that it planned to sell its remaining stake in SOCO and another London-listed affiliate to fund acquisitions.
